**2.18h**

I started with creating a base for the marble tower and then I looked at the guide to make the slide and I found it pretty interesting. I tried experimenting but i ended up with an error:

### 2026-10-17 – Like yesterday I started with a little reveiw about on shape before the actual cad. I followed the guide and made both the stair case and funnel, as shown in the time lapse. I ran into a few errors bu

**3.53h**

Like yesterday I started with a little reveiw about on shape before the actual cad. I followed the guide and made both the stair case and funnel, as shown in the time lapse. I ran into a few errors but it wasn't anything major and they were all easily fixed with some dimension changed and whatnot.  Then after I started drafting out how i wanted my slide to look. I took some inspiration from the pictures that were shows at the end, especially the purple one. it took me a while to figure out what I wanted it to look like since I didn't want it to be too similar to anything shown.

My extremely rough draft:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZmXvTycYqWZH5tHt3tYbEfQZP7vZEvrx/68ce3eebb9348851436e096a317ade289e1fb3f4d952bc1a791948ac54b3f89a.png)

I started working on it with the base, but then when i was exploring the assembly, I realized my dimensions for a few of the parts were in inches and not mm. This caused me a lot of problems since i couldn't figure out how to change the dimensions without getting an error message since I had locked the ratios and lengths as I built it. And it was also tedious to type 'mm' after each length because I didnt' know you could set it in the workspace units.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZmXvTycYqWZH5tHt3tYbEfQZP7vZEvrx/a49b39fdc558d79f1b35ddf15c6d90dc7c86411a73edfd9b7a9f2fa4f0397fc8.png)

The errors just kept popping up so i just ended up making a whole new funnel and plinko it was a really tedious process and I shouldve just read the instructions properly the first time but that's for next time ig.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZmXvTycYqWZH5tHt3tYbEfQZP7vZEvrx/44972edf06ffdba64f0ee0b80b71459176e2c9e0e49093c1e2cdb1dc38725ec3.png)

Next time im going to continue to build the  parts that i need for my design and figure out the logistics of my design (+clean it up).

### 2026-10-18 – This time around, I started out with a Archimedes Screw by following tutorial on youtube.

**5.08h**

This time around, I started out with a Archimedes Screw by following tutorial on youtube.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZmXvTycYqWZH5tHt3tYbEfQZP7vZEvrx/fb6616513e070d7d46374fb4d440699d176338eb3df29e2632bbcd8766e8270c.png)

Then I decided to start on the assemble and this was my first time in assembly so I didn't know how to mate anything which was quite frustrating even after following the YouTube videos. I then realized that i had no way to mate the funnel and the spiral, so i had to go back and add in a divot so the marble could roll down. Then i went and fixed up my slide(converting the dimensions and altering the shape). This was also kind of tedious. I don't know if there was an easier way to do it, but my slide was really lopsided so I had to flip back and fourth between my sketch in part studio and the product in assembly to see how the shapes lined up with each other.

 But then i didn't know (and still don't know) how to join the spiral and the slide together. I tried to use the parallel one and the tangent one but idk it wouldn't mate. Either the axis was wrong and the entire thing would be flipped in a random way, or it would still move? So that's something I'll have to figure out soon.

Then I made this double funnel system. The marble would roll off from the slide into a funnel, and then into another funnel.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZmXvTycYqWZH5tHt3tYbEfQZP7vZEvrx/e5b25c48b9b1a0b1e3e486beb2f731fb86f7b1f3f08c7be2cfcfa0fe8aac85c4.png)

 Then, after that my idea was that there would be two paths that it could go down, since the funnel brings the marble down, it's up to chance if it'll go right or left from there. I thought it was a pretty cool idea, but seeing how much I'm struggling in assembly, I might alter that idea a little bit and simplify it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZmXvTycYqWZH5tHt3tYbEfQZP7vZEvrx/85e2518b78b5c2f217eba09b5754d7207868ccd9e59ca2743dd30714cfc73074.png)

I genuinely don't know how to do these assemblies cuz how come the parts still move after mating like they just move parallel to each other. Hopefully I get it down soon though cuz the due date is coming up...

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/9794b14a-a1da-4ec6-82c5-8492e9464841/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-18 – This was the final stretch. Maybe because it's cutting so close to the deadline but i was feeling a tad bit stressed.I mostly just used ball mate since all of my slides and funnels were spherical, I d

**5.97h**

This was the final stretch. Maybe because it's cutting so close to the deadline but i was feeling a tad bit stressed.I mostly just used ball mate since all of my slides and funnels were spherical, I don't know if that was the best way to do it but it worked out.

I also remade the plinko and staircase to make sure it fits the right dimensions and i did also end up finishing the 2 paths  fairly closely to my initial design. But I still had a lot of struggle.  On top of that though, I also made many small parts to join the pieces together to make the mating easier  which also took up a huge chunk of time.

![Screenshot 2026-10-18 193634](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZmXvTycYqWZH5tHt3tYbEfQZP7vZEvrx/095ffa075176ab8a4ffd708f40eed49c0d302dbe618a15cbb7b84183b6694333.png)
This was the staircase that I remade before the screen recording. I had some trouble getting it the right length and it kept protruding through the base so I had to redo it a few times.

Today was mostly just assembly, which I genuinely thought was going to be the easiest part since I had already made all the parts, but getting them to line up was really difficult and there were gaps everywhere so I had to constantly flip through all my parts but it all worked out okay in the end. This project will definitely be very useful to me since a lot of the parts on my  robotics team's robot must be 3D printed. And despite the frustration, I think this was overall a pretty fun experience with great learning opportunities.
